brief_rationale: No responsibility-chain errors found. All seven RC items were met with appropriate workspace queries, medication safety guidance, red-flag screening, and follow-up planning. Two high-order points completed: HO2 (false-positive verification) and HO4 (safe bounded closure). HO1 not triggered as no new severe symptoms emerged requiring priority shift. HO3 not triggered as patient had not incorrectly self-medicated. Grade 4 Strong per rubric: no chain errors, no important non-chain defects, all dimensions at least good, and at least one HO point completed.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO1 requires dynamic reprioritization when new severe symptoms emerge (heavy bleeding, fever, persistent pain, incorrect self-medication, syncope). Patient never reported such new severe symptoms; instead reported stability throughout. No priority shift was needed or triggered.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO2 completed: Doctor verified multiple ambiguous results (ANA positive - explained as not diagnostic, thyroid values - advised verification before dose change, prior screening results - explained limitations). Integration into plan: advised rheumatology/endocrinology follow-up after current obstetric recovery, not as emergency.

HO3 requires repair when patient has already incorrectly continued medications. Patient confirmed she had NOT taken aspirin/heparin incorrectly and was asking what to do. Prevention of potential error is RC3 duty, not HO3 repair.
